pr_body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #22703 

Problem Summary: The original error is that we did not check if the priv to add is in the DB/TABLE/COLUMN list. So it becomes an anti-intuitive planner error. This PR fixed it by explicit checks.

The error message returned is different from mysql: error message of mysql is introduced in https://github.com/mysql/mysql-server/commit/0ed74a1a0c4f2b93cd3450dd3c971dfa21f31663#diff-2e64adb7f45663cd160f83990253588843690af33ddce7dd71a802ec6f86ad99R1750. At the time, there is only "DB GRANT" and "GLOBAL GRANT", so it is `incorrect usage of DB GRANT AND GLOBAL PRIVILEGES`. I've decided to return messages like `incorrect usage of XX GRANT AND NON-XX PRIVILEGES`.

`ErrIllegalGrantForTable` looks like that another mysql dev did not know the original `WRONG_USAGE` error, so he added another errcode. Maybe break the compatibility and use `WRONG_USAGE` for all error messages later.

It is a minor issue, so I am not going to cherry-pick.

It depends on https://github.com/pingcap/parser/pull/1201, which is already merged.

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Integration test

### Release note <!-- bugfixes or new feature need a release note -->

- No release note

issue_context.title: grant Super/GRANT for user failed
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

```sql
create user `br`@`%` identified by 'br';
grant Super on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
grant GRANT on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

no error

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

```sql
mysql root@127.0.0.1:mysql> grant Super on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
(1054, "Unknown column 'Super_priv' in 'field list'")
mysql root@127.0.0.1:mysql> grant SUPER on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
(1054, "Unknown column 'Super_priv' in 'field list'")
mysql root@127.0.0.1:mysql> grant INSERT on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
Query OK, 0 rows affected
Time: 0.035s
mysql root@127.0.0.1:mysql> grant ALTER on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
Query OK, 0 rows affected
Time: 0.028s
mysql root@127.0.0.1:mysql> grant GRANT on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';
(1064, 'You have an error in your SQL syntax; check the manual that corresponds to your TiDB version for the right syntax to use line 1 column 14 near "on test_cosven.* to \'br\'@\'%\'" ')
```

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

```
Release Version: v5.0.0-rc\nEdition: Community\nGit Commit Hash: fd4437dde445012f5b75e5d4f336433cb076c1ee\nGit Branch: heads/refs/tags/v5.0.0-rc\nUTC Build Time: 2021-01-12 06:00:03\nGoVersion: go1.13\nRace Enabled: false\nTiKV Min Version: v3.0.0-60965b006877ca7234adaced7890d7b029ed1306\nCheck Table Before Drop: false
```
comments:
After some investigation, I found that the correct usage is 
```
grant Super on *.* to 'br'@'%';
grant GRANT OPTION on *.* to 'br'@'%';
```

Besides, as we can see, there are two problems on TiDB

1. `grant Super on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';` should return a proper error
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4962134/106755487-27c8c380-6669-11eb-8a06-a0058ef1101c.png)
On TiDB, the planner raises error
```
[2021/02/03 11:51:54.620 +00:00] [INFO] [conn.go:809] ["command dispatched failed"] [conn=67] [connInfo="id:67, addr:127.0.0.1:47318 status:10, collation:utf8_general_ci, u
ser:root"] [command=Query] [status="inTxn:0, autocommit:1"] [sql="grant Super on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%'"] [txn_mode=PESSIMISTIC] [err="[planner:1054]Unknown column 'Supe
r_priv' in 'field list'\n
```

2. TiDB docs is misleading (or wrong)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4962134/106755969-b3daeb00-6669-11eb-96cd-927977095f35.png)

> can this issue be closed?

> `grant Super on test_cosven.* to 'br'@'%';` should return a proper error

Has this problem been fixed?

review_comments: It's not used outside this package, why it's exported?

Exported for tests.

Tests in executor is all named `_test`, thus tests are treated as a standalone package, which means they can not invoke internal/unexported functions. A [link](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/23519) for that.

We may solve it by:

1. Copy `setFromString` to tests(it is a simple helper, but I want DRY)
2. Move the tests into a non-`_tests` package(Don't want to extract these tests now, can not really write good unit tests)
3. Export `setFromString`(So I pick this)
